--- `00 / spec` | field | value | |:--|:--| | **version** | `0.1.0` | | **host** | OpenCode `2.x` · `1.19.x` fallback | | **default model** | `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | | **tests** | `52 passing` | | **license** | `MIT` | ## a swarm, not a chat room/ One goal goes in. A plan comes out. Workers run in parallel, claim their files, message each other, and the orchestrator only wakes up for decisions that matter. When the work is done it verifies the result and closes the swarm with evidence. It is **goal-driven, supervised autonomy** — not a daemon, not a sandbox, and not a chat room where agents politely take turns. | # | what | why | |:--|:--|:--| | `01` | **parallel by default** | Multiple child sessions work at the same time, each with its own role and model. | | `02` | **file-safe** | Plan-time write-sets, file leases, and content-hash checks. No lost updates. | | `03` | **peer messaging** | Workers talk directly. The orchestrator sees digests, not every message. | | `04` | **low-friction reviews** | Routine spawns are automatic; only real escalations reach the orchestrator. | | `05` | **supervised recovery** | Stale locks, idle workers, retries, budgets, and completion are handled deterministically. | | `06` | **evidence before done** | Tasks close with commands, exit codes, and a summary — not a vibe. | --- `01 / install` ## install/ | requirement | detail | |:--|:--| | **opencode** | `2.x` — tested on `2.2.0`. `1.19.x` works through the V1 loader. | | **runtime** | [Bun](https://bun.sh) `1.4+` | | **model** | Any tool-capable provider. OpenCode Go is the default, not a requirement. | ```bash git clone https://github.com/DumDuky/opencode-swarm.git cd opencode-swarm bun install ``` **Global** — every chat, every project. Add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": [ { "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-swarm", "options": {} } ], "instructions": [ "/absolute/path/to/opencode-swarm/docs/SWARM.md" ] } ``` **Project** — one repo only. Put the same `plugins` entry in that project's `opencode.json`. ```bash opencode reload opencode plugin list # should list opencode-swarm ``` Then, from any chat: ```text /swarm Add a health endpoint with tests ```
V1 fallback (OpenCode 1.19.x) Copy [`examples/local-plugin/swarm.ts`](examples/local-plugin/swarm.ts) into `.opencode/plugins/swarm.ts` and restart OpenCode. V1 also registers dedicated agents: `swarm`, `swarm-worker`, `swarm-tester`, `swarm-scout`, `swarm-reviewer`, `swarm-planner`, `swarm-integrator`.
From npm Not published yet. Once it is, the entry becomes `{ "package": "opencode-swarm", "options": {} }`.
--- `02 / the cast` ## roles/ Seven roles, one runtime. Every spawn is a real child session with its own model, brief, and file write-set. | # | role | default model | job | |:--|:--|:--|:--| | `01` | **orchestrator** | `flash` | Plans the board, spawns workers, reviews escalations, closes with evidence. | | `02` | **worker** | `flash` | Owns a task and a write-set. Claims files, edits, tests, reports. | | `03` | **tester** | `flash` | Runs the commands, checks acceptance, writes the proof. | | `04` | **scout** | `flash #low` | Read-only reconnaissance before anyone touches the repo. | | `05` | **reviewer** | `flash #high` | Reads the diff against the plan. Approves or sends it back. | | `06` | **planner** | `flash #high` | Turns a vague goal into disjoint tasks with dependencies. | | `07` | **integrator** | `flash #high` | Runs the full gate, resolves the seams, prepares the summary. | V2 reuses the built-in `build`, `general`, and `explore` agents with role instructions. V1 registers dedicated agents. --- `03 / the hard part` ## no-lost-updates/ Parallel agents are easy to demo and hard to trust. Three layers keep the workspace consistent, and a fourth keeps the bill honest.

| layer | what it does | |:--|:--| | **partition** | Open tasks cannot claim the same files unless one depends on the other. | | **leases** | A worker must own a file or directory before editing it. TTLs expire stale claims. | | **hashes** | If the file changed since the last read, the edit is rejected and must re-read. | | **budget** | Cost warns, then pauses. Member, depth, and concurrency caps are separate. | Same-file edits serialize. That is intentional. Worktree isolation and a merge queue are the next major addition. --- `04 / the interface` ## surface-area/ Five commands, ten tools, five config groups. That is the whole API. | command | purpose | |:--|:--| | `/swarm ` | Start a swarm, or resume a paused one. | | `/swarm-status` | Members, tasks, leases, approvals, budget. | | `/swarm-stop` | Stop the swarm and interrupt workers. | | `/swarm-approve [reason]` | Approve a pending escalation. | | `/swarm-deny [reason]` | Deny a pending escalation. | | tool | purpose | |:--|:--| | `swarm_start` | Create the swarm and become the orchestrator. | | `swarm_task` | Create, list, claim, update, or release tasks. | | `swarm_spawn` | Spawn a worker, tester, scout, reviewer, planner, or integrator. | | `swarm_message` | Send, broadcast, read, or wait for messages. | | `swarm_files` | Claim, release, or list file leases. | | `swarm_status` | Compact swarm dashboard. | | `swarm_wait` | Wait for members or tasks, return summaries. | | `swarm_finish` | Finish a task or close the swarm with evidence. | | `swarm_review` | Orchestrator-only approval queue. | | `swarm_stop` | Stop one member and its subtree, or the whole swarm. | --- `05 / receipts` ## proof/ | tests | lost updates | default budget | health run | |:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:| | **52** | **0** | **$3.00** | **3/3** | Real runs, recorded in [`docs/e2e-demo.md`](docs/e2e-demo.md): - **Parallel build** — two workers, one dependency-gated tester. 3/3 done. - **Dynamic write-set** — a tester needed a file outside its set, asked, and the board re-validated the expansion. 2/2 done. - **Role agents** — session export confirmed the child ran under `swarm-worker`, not the parent agent. - **V2 host** — same core through the V2 adapter, positive and negative cases re-run by the orchestrator. - **Health endpoint** — `node --test` 4/4, live `200`, unknown path `404`. --- `06 / config` ## config/ V2: put these in the `plugins` entry options. V1: use `swarm.config.json`. ```jsonc { "models": { "orchestrator": "opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash", "worker": "opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash", "scout": "opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash#low", "reviewer": "opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash#high", "planner": "opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash#high", "tester": "opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash", "integrator": "opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash#high" }, "limits": { "maxMembers": 8, "reviewAtMembers": 6, "maxDepth": 2, "maxConcurrent": 4, "maxMessagesPerMinute": 10, "maxMessageLength": 4000, "maxTaskAttempts": 2 }, "budget": { "maxCostUsd": 3, "maxTokensPerTask": 0, "warnAt": 0.7, "pauseAt": 0.9 }, "leases": { "ttlMs": 600000, "autoClaim": true }, "approval": { "mode": "balanced", "timeoutMs": 120000, "onTimeoutMedium": "allow", "onTimeoutHigh": "deny" } } ``` `maxTokensPerTask: 0` disables the per-task token guard. Cost is tracked separately. Set `models.orchestrator` to `"inherit"` to follow the session model. **Approval modes** — `balanced` (default) auto-allows routine work and reviews sub-subagents, directory leases, thresholds, and budget warnings. `strict` reviews more. `permissive` reviews less. --- `07 / questions` ## questions/
Do I need OpenCode Go? No. Any tool-capable provider works. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on OpenCode Go is the default because it is cheap and fast at this task shape.
Can two workers edit the same file? Not concurrently. Overlapping write-sets are rejected at plan time, leases serialize whatever still collides, and the hash guard refuses stale writes.
What stops a runaway swarm? A cost budget with warn and pause thresholds, plus member, depth, concurrency, and message-rate caps. `/swarm-stop` interrupts everything immediately.
Does it run forever on its own? No. It stops when the board is done, when you stop it, when the budget is hit, or when a limit is exceeded. It will not invent new goals.
Is it a sandbox? No. Workers run with the permissions OpenCode gives them. Destructive shell commands are blocked or escalated, but interpreters and repo content are still dangerous. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md).
--- `08 / examples` ## examples/ | example | shows | |:--|:--| | [`tiny-demo`](examples/tiny-demo) | Two parallel workers plus a dependency-gated tester. | | [`dynamic-write-set`](examples/dynamic-write-set) | A worker asks the orchestrator to expand its write-set. | | [`cwd-independent-check`](examples/cwd-independent-check) | Cwd-independent verification with a tester. | | [`health-endpoint`](examples/health-endpoint) | An HTTP health endpoint with Node tests and a live verification report. | --- `09 / develop` ## build-it/ ```bash bun install bun run check # tsc --noEmit && bun test ``` ```text src/ index.ts dual V1/V2 entrypoint service.ts orchestration, spawn, wait, approvals, supervision board.ts tasks and plan validation bus.ts messages, rate limits, loop detection leases.ts file leases, TTLs, content hashes policy.ts spawn/file/shell risk policy v1/ V1 plugin, runtime, tools, agents, state v2/ V2 plugin, runtime, tools, commands test/ board.test.ts bus.test.ts leases.test.ts policy.test.ts service.test.ts ``` The core depends on a narrow `SwarmRuntime` interface, so orchestration stays testable with [`test/fake-runtime.ts`](test/fake-runtime.ts). Issues and PRs are welcome — see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md). **Roadmap** — worktree isolation and a merge queue, a TUI dashboard, npm publishing, richer plan validation. --- `10 / limits` ## honest-limits/ - Shared workspace only. Worktree isolation and a merge queue are planned. - Same-file edits serialize by design. - No cross-machine distribution. - Not a security sandbox. Use workspace permissions and `/swarm-stop`. - The orchestrator is an LLM. The supervisor handles routine recovery, but plan quality still matters. - V1 ignores model variants; V2 supports them. ---

# Health endpoint example

A minimal HTTP server exposing a `/health` endpoint, built with the Node.js
standard library only. No dependencies, no build step.

## Run

```sh
node server.js
```

With no `PORT` set, the server binds an ephemeral port and prints the port it
actually got as a single line on stdout:

```console
$ node server.js
53142
```

Set `PORT` to pick the port yourself:

```sh
PORT=3000 node server.js
```

On Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:PORT = 3000; node server.js
```

Stop it with `Ctrl+C`; the process exits on `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`.

The examples below assume `PORT=3000`.

## Endpoint contract

### `GET /health`

Returns the service health snapshot.

- **Status:** `200 OK`
- **Content-Type:** `application/json`

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "service": "opencode-swarm",
  "uptime": 12.345
}
```

| Field     | Type     | Meaning                                      |
| --------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `status`  | `string` | Always `"ok"` while the process is serving.  |
| `service` | `string` | Service identifier, always `"opencode-swarm"`. |
| `uptime`  | `number` | Seconds the process has been running.        |

Any other path returns `404 Not Found` with a JSON body. Non-`GET` requests to
`/health` are also answered with `404`, so `GET` is the only supported method.

```json
{ "error": "Not Found" }
```

## curl example

```sh
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:3000/health
```

Expected response:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"status":"ok","service":"opencode-swarm","uptime":1.234}
```

Unknown paths:

```sh
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:3000/nope
# HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

## Test

The tests use the built-in `node:test` runner and `node:assert`, so nothing needs
to be installed. From this directory:

```sh
node --test server.test.js
```

Or from the repository root, where the quoted glob keeps the shell from expanding it:

```sh
node --test "examples/health-endpoint/*.test.js"
```

The suite starts the server on an ephemeral port (`0`), so it never collides with
a server you already have running, and closes it when the run finishes.

# Changelog

## 0.1.0

Initial release.

### Added

- `/swarm <goal>` command and `swarm_start` tool.
- Task board with plan-time write-set validation, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
- Parallel child sessions with per-role agents and models.
- File leases, TTLs, reentrant claims, directory/file conflicts, and content-hash stale-write checks.
- Peer message bus with direct messages, broadcast, blocking waits, rate limits, and loop detection.
- Policy engine for spawn, file, shell, and approval risk.
- Orchestrator-only review queue for sub-subagents, directory leases, thresholds, and budget warnings.
- Deterministic supervisor for stale locks, idle workers, failures, retries, reassignment, budgets, completion, and persistence.
- Wake-up path for ready and blocked tasks so the orchestrator does not stall between turns.
- OpenCode Go defaults with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and per-role model overrides.
- V2 plugin entrypoint and V1 fallback loader.
- 52 tests covering the core and the health endpoint example.
- Four example projects and real validation runs.
- A self-contained health endpoint example with Node.js tests and a live verification report.
- A themed landing page and README built on one visual system: `#06070a` ink, teal `#2ee6c5`, violet `#9d7bff`.
- Matching banner, logo, architecture, and live-board assets for the repository and docs site.

# Contributing

Thanks for helping improve `opencode-swarm`.

## Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/DumDuky/opencode-swarm.git
cd opencode-swarm
bun install
```

## Checks

Run the full gate before opening a PR:

```bash
bun run check
```

That runs TypeScript and the Bun test suite. If you change behavior, add or update a test in `test/`.

## What to work on

Good first issues are labeled `good first issue`. Larger changes should start with an issue so the design can be discussed before implementation.

The highest-value areas right now:

- worktree isolation and a merge queue
- TUI dashboard for live swarm state
- better plan validation and conflict detection
- recovery and budget edge cases
- documentation and examples

## Design principles

- **The core stays host-independent.** `src/service.ts` depends on the narrow `SwarmRuntime` interface. Keep new orchestration logic testable with `test/fake-runtime.ts`.
- **Safety is a feature.** Do not weaken file leases, content-hash checks, approval gates, or budget limits without a clear replacement.
- **Keep the orchestrator low-friction.** Routine work should not require human approval.
- **No silent overwrites.** If a change makes concurrent editing less safe, document it and add a test.
- **Small, focused PRs.** Separate refactors from behavior changes.

## Pull requests

1. Fork the repo and create a branch.
2. Make the change with tests.
3. Run `bun run check`.
4. Open a PR using the template.
5. Link the issue it resolves.

## Commit style

Use short, imperative commits, for example:

```text
feat: add worktree merge queue
fix: wake orchestrator for unowned ready tasks
docs: add V2 install example
```

Please do not report vulnerabilities in public issues. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

# Security policy

## Supported versions

| Version | Supported |
|---|---|
| 0.1.x | Yes |

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please **do not** open a public issue for a security vulnerability.

Report it privately using GitHub's [private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/DumDuky/opencode-swarm/security/advisories/new), or contact the maintainer through GitHub ([@DumDuky](https://github.com/DumDuky)).

Include:

- affected version
- a reproduction or proof of concept
- the impact you believe it has
- any suggested mitigation

## Scope and expectations

`opencode-swarm` is an OpenCode plugin. It runs with the permissions OpenCode gives it and is **not a sandbox**.

Security-relevant areas include:

- file leases and stale-write checks
- worker permissions and subagent limits
- shell command classification
- approval escalation
- secrets or credentials in prompts, logs, or state
- prompt injection from repository content or peer messages

The plugin already blocks common shell file-write patterns for workers and blocks destructive system commands. Interpreter escapes, external tools, and repo content can still be dangerous. Treat untrusted repositories and untrusted models accordingly.

## Disclosure

Please give the maintainer a reasonable window to fix and release before public disclosure. Credit will be given unless you prefer to remain anonymous.

# Validation

These are real runs, not mocks. The goal each time was deliberately small so the orchestration, file safety, and verification paths could be checked end to end.

---

## Run 1 — parallel build (V1, OpenCode 1.19.4)

**Goal:** create a tiny demo with two files and a dependency-gated tester.

- The orchestrator created three tasks: `hello.js`, `test-hello.js`, and a tester task depending on both.
- Two workers wrote the two files in parallel.
- The tester verified both commands and wrote a report.
- The orchestrator independently re-ran the commands before closing.

```text
node examples/tiny-demo/hello.js
hello from swarm
exit 0

node examples/tiny-demo/test-hello.js
PASS: hello.js output matches
exit 0
```

- Result: **3/3 tasks done**
- Cost: about **$0.005** · ~96k tokens
- Model: `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`
- Artifacts: [`examples/tiny-demo`](../examples/tiny-demo)

---

## Run 2 — dynamic write-set expansion

**Goal:** create `out.txt` and a `check.js` validator with one worker and one tester.

The tester discovered it needed one file outside its original write-set. It did **not** write it. It asked the orchestrator, the orchestrator expanded the task, reset it to `todo`, and the board re-validated the new write-set against every other open task. The tester reclaimed the task and finished.

```text
node examples/dynamic-write-set/check.js
OK: out.txt matches
exit 0
```

- Result: **2/2 tasks done**
- Cost: about **$0.044**
- Artifacts: [`examples/dynamic-write-set`](../examples/dynamic-write-set)

This is the intended safety path: agents adapt, but the orchestrator owns write-set changes and the board re-checks them.

---

## Run 3 — role agents verified

A third run created a cwd-independent check with one worker and one tester. Exporting the worker session showed `"mode": "swarm-worker"` on its assistant messages, confirming the child actually ran under the role agent rather than the parent agent.

- Result: **2/2 tasks done**
- Artifacts: [`examples/cwd-independent-check`](../examples/cwd-independent-check)

---

## Run 4 — V2 (OpenCode 2.2.0)

The plugin was loaded from the global V2 `plugins` config and the `swarm_start` tool was called from an ordinary chat.

- Orchestrator: `build`
- Worker and tester: built-in `general` agents with role instructions
- Dependency gate: the tester spawned only after the worker finished
- Result: **2/2 tasks done**
- The orchestrator independently ran the positive case and the negative case:

```text
node check.js
exit 0

# copied to a temp directory with wrong content
node check.js
exit 1
```

---

## Run 5 — health endpoint (swarm on the plugin repo)

**Goal:** add a health endpoint with tests.

The repository is an OpenCode plugin, not an HTTP service, so the endpoint was
added as a self-contained example instead of changing the plugin runtime.

Plan:

- `t1` worker: `examples/health-endpoint/server.js`
- `t2` worker: `examples/health-endpoint/server.test.js` and `README.md`
- `t3` tester, depends on both: run the tests and verify the live endpoint

The two implementation tasks ran in parallel. The tester spawned after both
were done.

Result:

- **3/3 tasks done**
- `node --test examples/health-endpoint/server.test.js` -> **4 pass, 0 fail**
- Live `GET /health` -> `200` with `{"status":"ok","service":"opencode-swarm","uptime":<number>}`
- Unknown path -> `404` with `{"error":"Not Found"}`
- No other files changed by the verification task

Artifacts: [`examples/health-endpoint`](../examples/health-endpoint), including
[`VERIFY.md`](../examples/health-endpoint/VERIFY.md).

---

## What the runs demonstrate

- Parallel child sessions actually run.
- Dependency-gated tasks are not spawned early.
- File write-sets are enforced, including a deliberate expansion.
- Workers and testers complete and report.
- The orchestrator can wake, verify, and close the swarm.
- The same core works through both the V1 and V2 host adapters.

---

## Reproduce it

The example directories are self-contained. To run the plugin locally:

```bash
bun install
bun run check
```

Then follow the install instructions in the [README](../README.md) and start a small goal with `/swarm`.

# Swarm

A parallel agent swarm is available in every chat and every project.

- Start with `/swarm <goal>` or call the `swarm_start` tool with the goal.
- `/swarm` starts in the current chat and may switch to the configured orchestrator agent (`build` by default). Calling `swarm_start` directly keeps the current agent and adds the orchestrator role instructions.
- The orchestrator plans with `swarm_task`, spawns workers with `swarm_spawn`, waits with `swarm_wait`, and closes with `swarm_finish`.
- Do not use the built-in task/subagent tool in a swarm session. Use `swarm_spawn`.
- Routine spawns and file claims are automatic. The orchestrator reviews only escalations such as sub-subagents, directory leases, member/concurrency thresholds, and budget warnings.
- `/swarm-status` shows the swarm. `/swarm-stop` stops it.
- Use `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` by default. Change role models with the plugin options in `opencode.json` (V2) or `swarm.config.json` (V1).
swarm ok
swarm ok

# Verification: health endpoint

Independent verification of `server.js` against the acceptance criteria:

1. the automated test suite passes,
2. a live `GET /health` returns `200` with the expected JSON,
3. an unknown path returns `404`.

This file was the only artifact written by the verification task. `server.js`,
`server.test.js`, and `README.md` were not modified.
